title: Junta Airstrike on Vumkhum Village, Mindat Township Kills 8 Civilians Including 3 Children
detail: A Myanmar military airstrike on August 30, 2026 dropped four bombs on Vumkhum village near Mindat Town, Chin State — a resistance-held area roughly 120 miles south of the state capital Hakha — killing 8 civilians, including 3 children (two primary school students and a Grade 9 student), and wounding 15 others. The strike occurred amid an ongoing junta counteroffensive launched in mid-May across three Chin townships. The Chin People's Army said regime airstrikes have repeatedly hit non-military targets across southern Chin State, including homes, schools, medical clinics, and places of worship.

media.caption: Myanmar Now report on the August 30 airstrike that killed 8 civilians in Mindat Township, Chin State.

title: KIA-KPDF Coalition Seizes Junta Hilltop Outpost Near Zinbon, Shwegu-Sinkhan Road
detail: A joint Kachin Independence Army (KIA) and Kachin People's Defense Force (KPDF) coalition seized a junta hilltop outpost near Zinbon on August 30, 2026, neutralizing a position the regime had used to control the Shwegu-Sinkhan roadway. A local commander described it as a temporary, lightly fortified position rather than a hardened base, but said reclaiming it was strategically important to cutting junta access to the road. The seizure came as junta forces were separately trying to reopen the Irrawaddy River corridor for its Mandalay-Bhamo resupply flotilla, which had been stalled at Shwegu since a drone strike disabled its lead warship on August 29.

media.caption: The hilltop outpost near Zinbon, Shwegu Township, retaken by KIA-KPDF forces on August 30, 2026.
